This confirms a Koi Stealer-style client GUID (`30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`) beaconed with encoded/binary payload — consistent with the ETPRO signature. Enough evidence to finalize.

---

# Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (domain: bepositive.com) |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic to the domain controller) |

Domain controller for reference: WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 at 172.17.0.17 (00:23:ae:50:ba:fd) — handles DNS/LDAP/Kerberos for the victim; not itself compromised in observed traffic.

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). Attribution is **signature-confirmed**: the provided Suricata export contains `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (Event #3.1504, 48 hits) matching HTTP POSTs from 172.17.0.99 to 79.124.78.197. This is independently corroborated in the raw pcap by repeated `POST /foots.php` beacons to the same bare-IP host, an `application/octet-stream` / `Content-Encoding: binary` body carrying a stable client GUID (`30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`), a spoofed legacy IE7 User-Agent, and a lightweight `nginx` C2 responding `200 OK` with empty bodies — a classic stealer check-in pattern.

## Timeline (relative to capture start)
- t=159.998s (2024-09-04 17:35:11 UTC) — `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` to 79.124.78.197: initial registration/subid check-in.
- t=161.228s — `POST /index.php` to 79.124.78.197: follow-up check-in.
- t=155.9s onward through end of capture (~t=3561s) — sustained `POST /foots.php` beacons to 79.124.78.197 every ~60–90 seconds (48+ occurrences flagged by Suricata), each carrying binary-encoded data tagged with the same client GUID.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Command-and-control:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — Koi Stealer C2 (bare-IP HTTP host, POST/GET beacon target)

**URLs / URIs (host: 79.124.78.197):**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — recurring stealer check-in/exfil endpoint
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — initial affiliate/subid registration
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — follow-up POST check-in

**Client identifier embedded in C2 traffic:**
- `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` — stable GUID sent in every `foots.php` POST body, unique to this infected host

**User-Agent (malware traffic marker):**
- `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)` — spoofed legacy IE7 UA used only on C2 traffic, not on any legitimate browser flow in the capture

No malware binary/executable was captured being transferred over HTTP in this pcap (the `/foots.php` and `/index.php` HTTP objects extracted are empty or trivial — the delivery/drop stage is not present in this capture, only the post-infection C2 phase). No file hash for a malicious payload can be grounded in this evidence.

## Benign context (not indicators)
- `172.17.0.17` (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19, domain controller) — DNS/LDAP/Kerberos/SMB traffic is normal AD activity for the LAN, not malicious.
- `46.254.34.201` (TLS SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) — ordinary user web browsing, unrelated to the stealer traffic.
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org`, `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `www.bing.com`, `sso.godaddy.com` — Windows/Adobe/Microsoft telemetry, update, and CRL/OCSP background traffic.
- SMBv1/NTLMSSP/Kerberos alerts (`GPL NETBIOS SMB ...`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow`) are IDS false-positive-prone signatures triggering on normal legacy AD authentication traffic between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller — no exploitation evidence beyond the signature match.
